subject: Proposal: Staggered uplift + yearly true-up for capacity (DataSpring)
content:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@dataspring.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Staggered uplift + yearly true-up for capacity (DataSpring)

Hi Tom —

Great talking earlier. Attached is a concise proposal that aligns with your goals to lock pricing while keeping the ability to scale quickly over the next 36 months. Key idea is a staggered uplift schedule with an annual true-up and an optional auto-renew window. High-level: 

- 3-year agreement with annual review windows (yearly true-up on usage)
- Staggered uplift: baseline committed tokens per year + built-in uplift tranches that trigger at defined usage thresholds (10% and 25%)
- Frontloaded onboarding credits in year 1 for migration and evals
- 12% volume discount blended across committed capacity; additional discounts tied to earlier payment cadence
- Auto-renew opt-in with 30-day written notice and the ability to convert to month-to-month buffer for short bursts

I attached a schedule showing year-by-year committed units and suggested billing cadence. Can you confirm procurement/legal timeline and whether DataSpring needs a vendor questionnaire completed before we send an SOW?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[karthik_iyer@redwood.com]

[Attachment: Dataspring_Proposed_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)]

-----
On Sat, 1 Aug 2026 at 11:03 AM, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@dataspring.ai> wrote:

Thanks Karthik —

This looks promising. A few quick clarifications: 

1) For the staggered uplift, does the uplift tranche consume committed units first or bill as overage until the true-up? We want predictable unit economics for forecasting.
2) What controls would our platform team have to limit automatic uplift binges (e.g., a hard cap per month unless manual approval)?
3) Procurement will want the SOW and a sample invoice. Legal tends to push back on auto-renew clauses; can that be optional?

If you can send a version with those items called out, procurement will move faster.

—Tom
Tom Ellis
Head of Infrastructure | DataSpring Inc.

-----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@dataspring.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Staggered uplift + yearly true-up for capacity (DataSpring)

Tom —

Quick answers inline and attached an annotated schedule that maps triggering behavior to billing and the true-up flow. Highlights: 

- Uplift handling: uplift tranches are provisioned as 'soft capacity' and will convert to committed units at annual true-up unless you elect to purchase them early. During the year, they show as pre-authorized capacity (no immediate overage billing) unless you cross the hard cap.
- Hard cap option: we can enable a hard cap per month to block automatic uplift beyond X% of baseline; that requires an admin approval workflow (we've shipped this for other enterprise customers).
- Auto-renew: make it opt-in. We'll put language in the SOW that requires explicit opt-in and a 30-day opt-out window prior to renewal.

Attached: Dataspring_Proposed_Schedule.xlsx (annotated) — the spreadsheet breaks out committed units, uplift tranches, and a sample true-up calculation.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share a draft SOW for procurement this week.
2) Marissa: can you confirm whether we should propose annual invoices or quarterly billing with annual true-up?
3) Neha: can you flag any technical gating items we should call out for the hard cap + approval flow?

Karthik

[Attachment: Dataspring_Proposed_Schedule.xlsx (updated, xlsx, 48KB)]

-----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@dataspring.ai>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Staggered uplift + yearly true-up for capacity (DataSpring)

Tom / Karthik —

Thanks for the details. From a renewals/finance perspective I recommend: 

- Quarterly invoice cadence with an annual reconciliation (true-up) — keeps forecasting granular while preserving the annual settlement.
- Include a 90-day early-exit ramp clause limited to first 12 months (protects both sides during migration).
- We'll include a clause that any uplift triggered and converted at true-up will be prorated to the date of conversion.

Tom, procurement will likely want a one-page exec summary + SOW + sample invoice. Karthik, can you draft those and flag anything legal needs to redline? Sergio, I’m copying you for playbook enablement on CS handoff and onboarding credits.

Marissa Cole
Head of Renewals | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@dataspring.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Staggered uplift + yearly true-up for capacity (DataSpring)

Tom —

Technical notes on the hard cap / approval flow: 

- We’ll expose a tenant-level rate limiter tied to the baseline commit. The hard cap is enforced by the serving runtime; when reached, requests return a 429 with a clear error code and a delta message describing how to request a temporary uplift.
- Approval flow: we can integrate with your internal ticketing (ServiceNow/Jira) or use an admin UI in our console where an admin approves a temporary uplift window. The uplift window is tagged and audit-logged.
- True-up telemetry: we'll provide per-route token breakdowns and a reconciled CSV at the end of each year for accounting.

Happy to run a quick tech walkthrough with your platform team this week if helpful.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

-----
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@dataspring.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Staggered uplift + yearly true-up for capacity (DataSpring)

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clarity — this structure should work for us. Procurement asked that the SOW call out: 

- Billing cadence = quarterly with annual reconciliation
- Opt-in auto-renew with 30-day opt-out window
- Hard cap default set to baseline + 15% (we may adjust after onboarding)
- Audit logs & per-route breakdown required for year-end reconciliation

Please go ahead and send the SOW + sample invoice. Also, we need DocuSign-ready quote so procurement/legal can sign off; they prefer a single PDF per DocuSign envelope.

If you can get the SOW and DocuSign packet to procurement@dataspring.ai and cc me, we’ll triage quickly.

—Tom

[Attachment: DocuSign_Quote.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

-----
Notes / internal (no PII in attachments):
- Karthik to create SOW draft and attach DocuSign_Quote.pdf; include explicit opt-in auto-renew language.
- Finance to model 3-year blended revenue with 12% discount and quarterly invoices; Marissa to confirm revenue recognition playbook.
- CS handoff: Sergio to own onboarding credits and confirm audit log retention.
